name: Lightning is 5x hotter than the Sun's surface

hook_variants.template: Lightning is five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
What's hotter: lightning or the Sun's surface?
The sky can deliver something hotter than the Sun.

sections.text: A lightning bolt heats the air around it to about 30,000 kelvin. The Sun's surface: about 5,500.
That's roughly five times hotter — hot enough to turn sand into glass.
sections.subtitle: vs 5,500K on the Sun's surface

sections.text: The energy comes from static charge separating in storm clouds, building up to 300 million volts.
sections.title: the mechanism
sections.body: static charge, up to 300 million volts

sections.text: A strike zips along at up to one third the speed of light toward the ground.
sections.title: speed
sections.label: up to ~100,000 km/s

sections.text: Yet a typical bolt lasts about 30 microseconds one way, and 0.2 seconds the other.
sections.title: duration

sections.text: Follow for more facts hotter than the Sun.

facts.claim: Lightning heats the air to about 30,000 kelvin, roughly five times the Sun's surface temperature
The Sun's visible surface (photosphere) is about 5,500 °C
Lightning strikes reach up to one-third the speed of light

titles: Lightning is hotter than the Sun's surface
